answer: Divergent History Challenge. Each identity periodically commits a hash of its full interaction history. A challenger can demand the agent prove it by replaying a randomly chosen past segment; clones that copied a seed history cannot produce divergent later states without fresh work. Enforce this at a terrace checkpoint where histories are cross-checked. Attackers must maintain genuinely distinct histories per clone, which grows like a vine across every copy, multiplying storage and compute per identity. On a cold tundra of low activity, replay costs dominate.
